title: منع وميض خطأ المزامنة أثناء تنفيذ حذف الطالب الجاري
userObservation: PO reports about one second of a red Sync warning behind the final confirmation during successful deletion of a student with no educational history, followed by roster navigation. N95 original is separately accepted.

evidenceStatus.sourceDiagnosis: High-confidence causal path in the actual current source; timing and the user's exact installed-browser asset version were not independently recorded.

finding: A normal, live, protected student-lifecycle command is treated as an interrupted/unsafe Sync recovery. The durable checkpoint exists before the RPC by design, and the existing exclusive lock makes safeToContinueUnrelatedWork=false. Both are currently interpreted as immediate display failure without a distinction for a currently running operation.

sourceChain.fact: executeStudentLifecycle persists the exact studentLifecycleResume checkpoint, updates store.state.device, then calls confirmAndReconcile. A checkpoint here does not by itself mean a failure.
confirmAndReconcile executes the authoritative RPC and canonical reconciliation inside runStudentLifecycleExclusive.

coordinatorOperationalState returns error immediately when studentLifecycleResume exists. The lifecycle wrapper uses runCloudRestoreExclusive, which sets restoreRunning=true and emits syncing before awaiting the task.
The operational summary sets safeToContinueUnrelatedWork=false while restoreRunning or the checkpoint remains; this accurately protects concurrent writes.
safeToContinueUnrelatedWork=false is classified as fatal error immediately, bypassing the 90-second transient-transport presentation logic.

The same safe=false condition is treated as durable warning evidence; the policy returns strip=true and upgrades a non-error state to error. This is a second presentation decision, not a server failure.
Sync notifications refresh the read-only summary and paint the status strip while the student sheet stays open. This accounts for a banner behind the ongoing confirmation.
Successful canonical reconcile clears the checkpoint and refreshes Product state; the exclusive wrapper then releases its lock and schedules ordinary Sync.

After openStudentManagement resolves successfully, the action intentionally assigns location.hash to the preserved Teaching's roster (or classes fallback). No location.reload is present in this delete action; a full page reload was not observed.

minimalFix.objective: Represent a currently running, context-bound student lifecycle operation as neutral in-progress presentation. Preserve the checkpoint, all write exclusions, RPC/owner semantics, reconciliation, scheduling and resume behavior. A leftover checkpoint after completion/failure/reload must still require immediate visible recovery.
minimalFix.conditionalPath: src/lib/student-lifecycle.js only if passing a precise existing checkpoint identity into the existing exclusive wrapper is needed; no change to command, receipt or reconciliation semantics.
minimalFix.presentationContract: Track live operation lifetime internally, bound to the current owner/workspace and exact active checkpoint/operation. Expose only privacy-safe status metadata, not owner IDs, mutation envelopes or raw records. While that exact operation is active and no independent hard error exists, present syncing/pending neutrally with cloudSyncHealthy=false. Keep safeToContinueUnrelatedWork=false and the existing Product write guard unchanged.
minimalFix.policyReason: sync-warning-policy really consumes the same unsafe boolean and currently emits strip=true/status=error even if the incoming state is syncing. A projector-only change may be re-projected later by app.js, but it still leaves a contradictory warning decision. Reuse the same explicit in-flight predicate in this existing policy; no new banner, timer, framework or UI surface is needed.
minimalFix.hardPrecedence: Durable failed/rejected/blocked work, revoked Auth, wrong owner/workspace, genuine hard failure, unknown unsafe state and checkpoint without a matching live operation retain their existing immediate visibility. The in-flight exception expires synchronously in finally and on owner/workspace change. It is not a grace period or blanket suppression while any sheet is open.
unchangedByScope: Student deletion eligibility, SQL, Auth and server receipts

checks.name: student_lifecycle_inflight_presentation
checks.scope: Use the real current coordinator/lifecycle client with the existing synthetic backend. Hold the RPC response or reconciliation behind a deterministic promise barrier. While the exact checkpoint and live exclusive operation are active, assert neutral summary/badge, no error status strip, cloudSyncHealthy=false, safeToContinueUnrelatedWork=false and Product edits still blocked. Do not solve by adding a sleep or changing retries.

checks.name: student_lifecycle_recovery_visibility
checks.scope: On the same focused harness, fail/interrupt the operation so its durable checkpoint remains but no live operation does; assert immediate visible recovery/error. Preserve the existing N95 hard-category assertions for failed/rejected work, Auth/owner and generic unsafe state, including context change. No full project suite.

checks.name: student_delete_confirmation_navigation
checks.scope: One bounded existing student-lifecycle browser case on real Product DOM with synthetic intercepted backend only: preview -> confirm -> held request -> successful receipt/reconcile -> success copy -> explicit Return -> expected originating roster. Observe the strip continuously during the held phase. Confirm no document reload or premature navigation. Reuse the existing navigation unit test. No live student deletion or new A/B Auth provisioning.

validationPlan.limitation: Existing N95 tests explicitly cover an orphan synthetic checkpoint and generic safe=false, but do not cover a checkpoint inside a genuine in-flight lifecycle. Add that missing distinction; do not weaken the orphan test. Browser/native fixture setup may reuse the already installed local PostgreSQL capability; no Docker or paid service is required.
